namedConstants.revealMath: StoryCaptions.tsx reveals one character per 34 ms. L1 is 94 chars = 3.196 s, so the 4.5 s slot is reveal plus read and the timer path provably cannot interrupt. L2 is 66 chars = 2.244 s, inside the 3.0 s slot, so L3 never interrupts L2. L3 is 58 chars = 1.972 s.
namedConstants.derivedRevealRule: revealSeconds(line) = line.length * 34 ms, computed from the frozen string constant at runtime. Nothing in the guards is a hardcoded reveal figure, so editing a frozen string can never let a slot silently outrun the line it protects.

contractInterpretation.summary: The repair commission paraphrased the seeding condition as "phase already non-surface OR anchors already active". Implemented per frozen acceptance criterion [20], which is phase-only. The disjunctive reading would reintroduce vd-01 exactly: chain-launch-anchor-fine-trace.json shows the chained route entering ch8-launch at t=5641 ms with anc.launch.ignition and anc.launch.liftoff ALREADY in activatedAnchorIds while the raw phase is still surface, so seeding on active anchors would consume the whole ladder on the very route the repair exists to fix. On a genuine mid-flight restore both conditions hold anyway, so phase-only is the only reading that is both contract-faithful and defect-free.

The commission described extending "an existing emission-trace mechanism the verifier consumes". No such mechanism exists in runtime code: the verification probes bridge modules directly through the Vite ESM graph (storyText, objectiveDirector, spaceFlight, signedSceneAvRuntime) and stamp their own events. l2Cause, l2DueAt, t_calibrationReceipt and t_M7Anchor are derived scheduling facts that no store exposes. Implemented as a new read-only snapshot getter, getEmergentStoryVoiceDiag(), in the allowed director file — the same shape the probes already bridge for getSignedSceneAvDebugSnapshot. It creates no state, drives nothing, and adds no persistence. Recorded as a created rather than extended surface so the verifier knows to bridge it.
